narrative.summary: UNICEF has issued guidance on AI and children setting out requirements for child-centred AI for governments and businesses. The first draft appeared in 2020, version 2.0 in November 2021, and version 3.0 in December 2025, which sets ten requirements covering regulation and oversight, safety, data protection, fairness, transparency and children's well-being.

instruments.summary: UNICEF's current guidance on AI and children. It recommends that governments and businesses meet ten requirements for child-centred AI: regulatory frameworks, oversight and compliance; safety; data and privacy protection; non-discrimination and fairness; transparency, explainability and accountability; respect for human and child rights; children's best interests and well-being; inclusion; preparing and empowering children; and an enabling environment. It is accompanied by a checklist.
instruments.current_status: Published by UNICEF Innocenti in December 2025 as version 3.0 of its guidance, following version 2.0 (2021) and a 2020 draft.
instruments.evidence_reference: '3.0 | DECEMBER 2025' printed in PDF; page also lists December 2025. Month only, so date given as 2025-12. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Version 3.0 (December 2025), ten requirements and checklist confirmed; draws on the CRC.; Page does not say 'non-binding' or discuss States' duties under the CRC.

It followed a 2020 draft and pilot testing.

membership_note: UNICEF is a United Nations fund without separate membership; it is governed by a 36-member Executive Board elected from UN Member States.

members_source.comment: UNICEF is a fund of the United Nations created by the General Assembly; it is governed by an Executive Board of 36 Member States elected by ECOSOC and serves all UN Member States. It has no separate membership. Read 2026-10-21.
